segments.translation_text: One should delightedly armor oneself to the performance of long periods of hardship to achieve the profound purpose. Wearing the armor of great diligence, one should resolutely apply oneself to the great purpose, which is the accomplishment of vast benefit for oneself and others. One will accomplish the great result which is perfect enlightenment, Buddhahood. In brief, create the unique enlightenment thought, which is holding in one’s mind the primary goal of striving for great enlightenment for the purpose of sentient beings. The Mahayana Sutra Alankara states:

segments.translation_text: The paths of accumulation and application are the stage of engagement through motivation; they are also known as the stage of enlightenment thought that arises from motivation. Beginning from the path of seeing which is the first bumi, up to the path of meditation, which is the seventh bumi, is the stage of enlightenment thought which arises from the purification of benevolent thought. The three special stages of the path of meditation, which begins from the eighth bumi onward, is the stage of enlightenment thought which arises from the ripening result. The stage of Buddhahood, which is the accomplishment of the path of no more learning, is the stage of enlightenment thought which arises from the relinquishment of obscuration. These are the four stages of enlightenment thought. The Mahayana Sutra Alankara states:

segments.translation_text: Wishing enlightenment thought aims for the result of Buddhahood. Engaging aims for the cause of enlightenment, which is the path. Some other masters explain that wishing enlightenment thought occurs before reaching the irreversible stage and engaging occurs after reaching that stage.

segments.translation_text: The intent of Bodhisattva Shantideva is that even without being associated with a ritual, through the power of seeing the holy body of the Buddha and feeling compassion arise toward sentient beings, it is possible for one to wish to achieve perfect enlightenment Buddhahood, and to feel great sincerity toward that goal, which is known as wishing enlightenment thought. During the ritual, one receives the vow and engages in the conduct of the six perfections, and thus travels on the path of great enlightenment, which is known as engaging enlightenment thought. segments.translation_text: The above explanation shows that enlightenment thought is embodied in both wishing and engaging enlightenment thought. Concerning the vow, the Cheshitdu states that the nature of engaging enlightenment thought is to constantly engage one’s body, voice, and mind in the benefit of others, even without regard for one’s physical health and possessions. This summarizes the morality of the Mahayana path.

segments.wylie: de la dbye na spang bya mi dge ba mtha' dag spong ba sdom pa'i tshul khrims dang / gnyen po dge ba mtha' dag sgrub pa dge ba chos sdud kyi tshul khrims dang / byed las gzhan gyi don kho na byed pa sems can don byed kyi tshul khrims gsum mo/ /
segments.translation_text: If classified, there are three types of morality: abandoning all negativities that should be discarded is the morality of the vows of relinquishment; gathering every possible virtue as an antidote to negativity is the morality of acquiring virtuous Dharmas; the outcome of this is to act only for the benefit of other beings, which is the morality of performing others’ benefit.

segments.translation_text: It is possible that one may have enlightenment thought without having received the vow. An example is a person in whom wishing enlightenment thought has arisen, but this thought has not been developed through ritual and is not associated with conduct. However, it is not possible for one to have the vow without having enlightenment thought because all Mahayana vows must be associated with or sealed by enlightenment thought.

segments.translation_text: Extorting offerings to the Three Jewels; Abandoning the holy Dharma; Punishing the fully ordained and forcing them to disrobe; Indulging in the five heinous sins; and Holding wrong views are the five root downfalls (that occur for rulers).

segments.wylie: blo ma sbyangs pa la stong pa nyid ston pa dang / theg chen la zhugs pa phyir bzlog pa dang / so sor thar ba spangs te theg chen la sbyor ba dang / slob pa'i theg pas chags sogs spong ba min par 'dzin pa dang / rnyed bkur gyi phyir bdag la bstod cing gzhan la smod pa dang / rang nyid zab mo bzod par smra ba dang / dkon mchog gsum gyi dkor sbyin zhing len par byed pa dang / bsam gtan pa'i longs spyod kha ton pa la sbyin pa (phal ba la 'byung nye ba brgyad)la sogs spong zhing /
segments.translation_text: The eight root downfalls that occur for ordinary beings are: teaching the view of emptiness to those who have not trained their mind; causing those who have entered the Mahayana path to retreat; abandoning the path of individual liberation and engaging in the path of Mahayana; believing that the path of disciples is unable to produce relinquishment of attachment and the like; praising oneself and blaming others for the purpose of material gain; bragging that one is comfortable with profundity; giving and taking materials offered to the Three Jewels or giving the possessions of meditators to those who are only reciting prayers. Train in discarding these.

segments.wylie: ces pa ltar ro/ /de yang mtshan nyid pa ni sa dang po rab tu dga' ba la chos thams cad bdag med par mnyam pa nyid dang / sems can thams cad de'i rang bzhin can tu mnyam pa nyid dang / rang gzhan gyi sdug bsngal thams cad spang bar bya bar mnyam pa nyid dang / sangs rgyas thams cad la bdag nyid dang chos kyi dbyings su dbyer med par mnyam pa nyid rtogs pa las thob ste/
segments.translation_text: Genuine primordial wisdom of ultimate enlightenment thought only begins when one reaches the first Bodhisattva bumi of extreme joy. On this stage, one discovers all phenomena to be equally selfless, and that each and every sentient being possesses that nature equally. Also, one sees that all of one’s own and others’ sufferings need to be relinquished equally, and that the true nature of the realm of reality and the nature of all Buddhas are indivisible. With this realization, ultimate enlightenment thought is attained. It is said:
